title: Error Bounds for the Network Scale-Up Method

problem.claim: The Network Scale-Up Method estimates the size of a hidden sub-population in a social network from reports by queried network nodes about their neighbors.

gap.claim: Analytical bounds on Network Scale-Up Method estimation errors had not been proven.

contributions.claim: Provides analytical error bounds for the two most popular Network Scale-Up Method estimators.
Shows that adversarial network design and hidden-subpopulation placement can make the estimate differ from the real value by a factor of Ω(√n) in a network with n nodes.
Proves error bounds for randomly generated networks, including improved analytical bounds for Erdős-Rényi and Scale-Free networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The theoretical analysis is supported by an extensive set of numerical experiments examining how sample size affects estimate accuracy in synthetic and real networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The Network Scale-Up Method has been used for over thirty years to estimate hidden sub-population sizes in social networks.
The method queries a subset of network nodes about how many neighbors belong to the hidden sub-population and generally assumes favorable network structure and distribution.
Analytical error bounds for the method had not been proven.
The paper gives bounds for two popular estimators, including an adversarial Ω(√n) error factor and constant-factor high-probability guarantees for random networks with O(log n) samples.
Numerical experiments study the effect of sample size on accuracy in synthetic and real networks.

source_observation.claim: Estimator accuracy can deteriorate substantially when network structure and hidden-subpopulation placement are adversarial.

interpretation.claim: Error guarantees should account explicitly for structural assumptions rather than relying only on estimator behavior under well-behaved networks.

application.claim: When applying Network Scale-Up Method estimates, assess whether network topology and hidden-subpopulation distribution could violate the assumed conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the adversarial error factor applies to randomly generated networks.

source_observation.claim: Random-network guarantees can achieve a small constant factor with logarithmic-size samples and high probability.

interpretation.claim: Randomness in network generation may enable substantially stronger estimation guarantees than adversarial settings.

application.claim: For networks plausibly modeled by the analyzed random families, logarithmic sample sizes may be a useful design target for estimation studies.

exception.claim: These guarantees assume that queried nodes accurately report their degree and the number of hidden-subpopulation neighbors.

unknowns: Definitions of the two estimators are not provided.
The exact constants, probability statements, and conditions in the analytical bounds are not provided.
Numerical experiment results and sample-size effects are not quantified.
The abstract does not specify the real networks, synthetic configurations, or adversarial construction details.
